[b]Playing status:[/b] 100% achievement, 4x + playthroughs
[b]Grindy Achievement(s):[/b] No.
[b]Optional Achievement(s):[/b] Yes (16 achievements).
[b]Difficult Achievement(s):[/b] No.

[h1]Intro[/h1]
You found a lost phone. Inside, you find someone asking for help. [b]SIMULACRA[/b] puts you in the shoe of a stranger who is trying to find the owner of a lost phone. Will you succeed or will you fail?

[b]Pros:[/b]
- 4 endings with slight story branches
- New game plus let you play the game with faster chat speed

[b]Cons:[/b]
- No manual save and extra save slot to make it easier to unlock all endings
- Not suitable for people who have issues with flashing lights

[b]Specs[/b]
Intel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650

[h1]Should you buy this game?[/h1]
[b]Yes.[/b]
[i]If you like to read a visual novel that was told through phone and chats, feel free to buy this game at a sale.[/i]

[hr][/hr]
[h1]In-Depth Review[/h1]

[h3]Visuals[/h3]
As a game that is played out on a smartphone, the game does well to simulate the phone-like interface. It has a photo app, a contact book, a chat app - anything that you'll expect from a smartphone. Its functionality is limited tough. There is no option to switch between tabs nor a scroll bar on the right side of the screen to scroll the page faster.

[h3]Story[/h3]
The story is played out from series of chats. Expect a lot of typos and shortened words due to the informal context. This brings forth the characters' personality though, especially since everyone has a unique texting style from each other. Some information can also be retrieved by watching videos and receiving phone calls, although their voice is not expressive enough - it feels dragged out on purpose to make it easier for non-native English speakers to listen to. It does make them easier to hear, but it also kills their expression in the process.

Interface aside, the presentation helps with the storytelling. The glitchy screen and a few jumpscares help to set the mysterious vibe, while the surprising phone calls freak me out sometimes. It got toned down as you play the game, focusing more on the mysterious element. The writing was done well in regards to what's happening and sometimes, you will have several options to choose from. Despite giving the same outcome, the conversation will play out differently based on which option that you choose. However, some sentences are not flowing smoothly after choosing a certain option, giving you the impression that you chose the wrong one.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2466225479 

[h3]The Game[/h3]
[b]Gameplay[/b]
The gameplay is focused on chatting with people and exploring everything that is inside the phone that you used. As I said before, sometimes you will have to choose between several options to proceed. Some of them will affect the endings, some are not. Some old chat and photos will also be encrypted, allowing you to play a minigame to restore their state, which takes form in arranging photos or word. It's quite easy to finish although some words might be difficult to arrange sometimes.

Hints are usually provided whenever you are stuck. You can ask people to figure out what you are supposed to do and they will gladly help you out. However, I got stuck twice with no idea to proceed. Although one is expected since I never do well with puzzles that have vague rules, another feels like they don't give enough hints to solve.

[b]Length and Difficulty[/b]
I finished the game in ~4h, and proceed to replay the game several times to get all achievements. The new game+ helps a lot by providing a faster chat speed, allowing you to finish the game faster. However, you still need to wait for the voice-over near the ending to finish, and they talk very slowly. It was tiring to wait for them to finish talking and playing the game several times to unlock all four endings become not fun anymore. I wish there is an option to fast-forward the game at this point.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2466225684 

[b]Problems[/b]
Although the game has a phone-like interface, some quality of life features are missing, notably the option to switch tabs in the browser (or the option to keep existing tab), and the feature to start a video from a certain timestamp. There were also some occasions when I had to type some forms and I couldn't use the tab button in my keyboard to switch between text boxes. Lastly, there are some flashing lights near the ending - people who have issues with it might want to stay out of the game.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
For a visual novel game, it still can be enjoyed with people who don't like to read a wall of text. You might need to read a lot, but they are mostly in the form of short chats which shouldn't take long to finish. The story picks up an interesting topic that is enhanced with its mysterious vibe, and although the story feels weak at times, it still proves to be an enjoyable read.

This is a decent "choices matter" voyeuristic psychological thriller with the occasional horror elements (jump scares) that is a must play for horror fans and might be worth checking out on sale for people who like story rich games.  Here is what you need to know:
+Doing all interactions through the phone is very well done.
+Phone UI includes a menu of sorts that shows options of things to do next, and choices you have made.
+All character personalities and writing is well done, but...
-Some of the in-person acting via video seems weak, but part of it could be the inherent awkwardness of characters or their situations.
-The story doesn't seem to really branch out, as it seems more on rails than branching given that choices influence actions that contribute to the end result but don't have a notable impact on the story other than how characters react/feel about you.
-Your in-game surroundings/background and the rare background noises outside of the phone have no relevance to what is actually going on, other than to set a "mood" and randomly have the chance at jump scaring you.  IMO all jump scares should happen within the context of what is ACTUALLY happening, otherwise the other jump scares have faster diminishing returns.
?I don't know that I was compelled enough by the story to want to play through again at 3-4 hours length to get a different ending and see how they interact with me differently.

I'm surprised. I was expecting something maybe a little hokey or cheesy by the end but what I got was actually a surprisingly effective, creepy tech horror story.

It feels like it wouldn't be out of place as something from the first couple of V/H/S movies. It apes the whole unconventional found footage thing to a tee and despite the occasional spot of grammatical weirdness, it's extremely well made and polished, especially for like five bucks. The acting was reasonably good, the villain was out and out creepy and well done. You can't ask for more, really.

It's about the perfect length for this sort of thing (two to three hours), there's a few puzzles that take some thinking but nothing that's complete and utter nonsense logic and it's replayable and branching with plenty of hidden easter eggs. Kudos to the developers, I'm glad I found out this was a thing.

review_text_raw:
Messed up "Search through a random strange gal's phone" simulator with a decent length, combines disturbing stuff and jumpscares with a story based around choices, all actions taking place from one phone. From the developers of Sara Is Missing, and honestly, Simulacra is a pretty solid game.

The only real downside this game has that I can think of is if you dislike such type of games. This game is more of a visual novel where you spend a lot of the time looking through text and pictures. It is neither a "hide n run" nor a "survival" horror game, it is kept simple. 

However if you're looking for a more unique horror game than the standard horror types of games, I REALLY encourage you to give Simulacra a try.

I'm not one to write reviews, but this is an exception

This game is somewhat short. For $5 what are you expecting? But it does have replay value.

The story is very well made. I found myself unable to stop until I got to the bottom of the mystery and a game that keeps me glued is a good game.

The horror element is there in spades. Be prepared for jumpscares throughout, but know preparing means nothing, and you will still be scared shitless.

The hidden details are plentiful and I found myself discovering new intricacies on every playthrough.

All in all, this game was short and cheap, but I'm glad I bought it. It was well worth the money.

A psychological horror/mystery about invading others privacy and cyberstalking?  Talk about checking all my boxes at once!  I'm in!!!

Okay, so this is a little game about you having someone elses cellphone.  I beat it in a few hours, four maybe, and enjoyed the trip.  Everything you have to do in this game, you do with this cell phone.  You get to break into email accounts, search online registries for sex offenders, and catfish people, all in an attempt to find the ultimate truth.  It's like someone finally based a game off my hobbies.

So, the story is kind of linear, in that you work to unlock new areas of the mystery, piece by piece.  First, you get to play with texts and pictures, then you get enough information to open the email, then you can gather what you need to beat security questions...  I'd say the gameplay is about sifting through information to find what you need to move on.  You also get to talk to the phone owner's friends, and they help to move the plot along, or you can ask them for help if you get stuck.

I say it's linear, but there are actually several branching paths that probably all end up in the same place.  Do you know Telltale games?  Kind of like that...  We might make a different turn here and there, but we're all on the same road with a beginning, middle and end.  Example?  Okay, here's an example...  You need to find out some information from this person through text.  Do you own up, tell them you're a creepo reading through someone elses phone because they might be in trouble, or do you try to bluff your way through, pretending to be who you're not?  Make your choice and either way, life will go on.  I don't think you can get stuck.  Then at the end they have a nice little screen that says things like "You and 68% of players looked at the porn stash," just like a Telltale game.  (there was no porn stash...)

It's pretty creative storywise, and I'm not going to give anything away, but it looked like there were about 4 different endings, and I wouldn't be adverse to trying again sometime to see how things can change.  I only had two of them available to me, so I must have needed to do something else to unlock the others, and I'm not entirely sure what that is, which is good to me.  Means the game still has more meat to it.  It reminded me of another game I played called Her Story, and I didn't recommend that one because one play is all it's good for, but this one was more than double the length and I'd be happy to go again some day.

Scariness, it wasn't scary, but I'm pretty tough to phase.  It likes to make creepy noises in your headphones.  There's some image distortion, but I wouldn't call anything a jump scare, which is good, because those turn people off.

TL:DR I had fun.  Maybe you'll have fun too?  I hope I've given you enough information to know if you'll enjoy it too.  That's why I'm writing all this after all.

Simulacra is another game within the sara is missing universe. The first game was good but with new additions to a series brings new mechanics and fixes the short commings of the original, does this game do just that? I will be reviewing the game with a pro/ con style and end with my conclusion.

Pro:
     The game is very creepy. Now jumpscares are cheap and something I dont really enjoy but the game has ambient sound effects that are very spooky. Sometimes you may hear nocking at a door or a wisper or see the lights flicker in your field of view. Some are not really strong in spooking the player but the sound effects really sell the horror.

      The plot is good. Now this is pretty much a horror thriller game that delves with a deep mystery. The game throws you for many loops making you question who can you trust and how much information you should provide. You never know who is at the other end of that text message you recieved. The further you go the deeper the rabbit hole goes.

        The gameplay is simplistic. A game having a simplistic gameplay is nothing to fear. This is like playing a tale tell game where you get dialogue options but sometimes it effects the response of other players and the ending. There are branching paths but not many to get more than 2ish playthroughs. Still it is good to see that some choices creates a response that effect the story and feels a bit like a genuine response in a hypothetical world.

Con:
      There are some puzzles that are difficult. This game has quite a few moments that test memory and makes you search for clues to progress but some of these clues are very well hidden meaning in order to progress you might need to search the internet for the solution to save the frustration. It is a minor issue but i swear there is this one puzzle i could never solve.

Conclusion:
       In short this game is short but it is a blast to play. The story is creepy with atmoshere and has a great story. If you play the game for just a short ammount of time you will be hooked into finding out the truth. I can not reccomend this game enough for anything curious in the game. It is resonably priced in retrospect to how long the game is.

So... this is one of those game I already watched someone (Jacksepticeye) play it, but 7 years is a long time and I forgot the fun little details.

Cons
-Oml, Greg and Cassie's voice actors... that was rough listening to. Taylor's cringe shower serenade tipped into a con for me.
-Some of the word puzzles were a bit tricky
--Just having picture and word puzzles is a bit weird for a horror game like this... but without it, it isn't really a game, I guess.
-Someone needs to check on Ashley, she is always drunk texting Anna...
-Anna is wearing the same thing in each of her vlogs... lol.
--Speaking of, boom mic appearance in one of those vlogs, and a man that isn't one of the actors as well in the vlogs.
-I'm fine with all the horror ambiance... but seriously... knocking?! I could understand for one certain scene, but those knocking cues makes me pause the game and make sure no one is knocking like a maniac on my office. The subtle knocks are worse than the banging knocking.
-Ofc one of the photos is Anna in a towel, lol.
-The most unbelievable thing? Even in 2017, a phone with only 6 apps, 3 of which are e-mail, text, and phone, is completely mystifying, lol. The other three are Internet, Tinder, and Twitter.
-One bad interaction with a certain character, and there goes three of the four endings. Bummer.

Pros
-I mean... it is an award-winning story. It went off of Black Mirror's coat tails, but who cares?
-Apart from the lack of apps... the phone looks lived in. It's a crappy phone that you have to do puzzles to read texts that are sent to you, so there's that, lol.
--The pictures that are just in there to give atmosphere truly did the job... namely because it isn't just Anna in the same outfit like the vlogs, lol. Actually made me like Greg for a second...
-The horror is ear-screeching and visual and audio jumpscares... so... not terrible.
-Right length of game, roughly 3 to 3 and a half hours.
-Pretty nice detective game
-Aside from Taylor's serenade, him, Anna, and Ashley's actors contributed nicely to the story

Honestly, its the length that is making me recommend it the most. Short story, in and out, and it makes running for the other endings less of a trudge.

Length <3hrs

Simulacra is a Mystery game in which the player is in possession of a missing girl's phone. Using the contacts and apps on her phone you need to track down what happened to her.

Using her phone you will be looking through her life, personal messages and contracts. This will expose you to her life, how she interacted with her friends and colleagues, and what led up to her losing her phone. The transitions of the phone's main image really works well for bringing the horror into the exploration, while the missing information on her phone adds to the mystery between the events.

The puzzles were straight forward, as information I needed to access further parts of the phone easily stood out to me from when I read through her texts and messages. This helped from needing to search through every part of the phone for something I missed.

In all aspects Simulacra feels like a refinement of ‘Sara is Missing’. The texts are not as large and information felt like it was a lot simpler to find, making the game much more enjoyable to get through.

Overall I really enjoyed Simulacra, it may have what feels like weak acting and some moments of absurdity. Yet the character development is great, and looking back on her life and what led up to the moments, with the mystery behind the dating app really made the game intriguing.

Just finished my first playthrough of this game are here are my thoughts:

Pros:
*Length was good for the price
*Story kept me invested throughout
*Some truly creepy moments that made me think about how themes in the game relate to potential problems in the real world
*A few not-so-obvious puzzles that gave me a sense of satisfaction when I figured them out

Cons:
*Most of the puzzles are pretty weak and repetitive
*There were a couple times where I was having two different conversations with the same person at the same time in the same text thread. I would say this is a glitch thought should have been remedied by now.
*Game crashed three times on me, and my system is no slouch
*The acting is pretty cringe-worthy.
*Ending was pretty unsatisfying, but I can go back and try again I guess...

In the end I think it was definitely worth a couple bucks and was a refreshing departure from the usual.

man, this is a difficult one to review. initially i wanted to give this a thumbs down, but it's fairly quality for it's price (especially since it's on sale often).

the story starts off great, but devolves to relationship drama. the acting is bad (so bad that i ended up actively looking for bad endings my first playthrough). there are random jumpscares for no reason. and the game is short, about 2-3 hours.

but this game is fairly entertaining and a decent value. the U/I is great, sound effects are fantastic, and gameplay is engaging. if you're curious, get it on a sale. not the best game, but definitely worth checking out.
